newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 2.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 2.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
SEATTLE - Cigarette advertising on billboards will be banned in much of Seattle under health regulations aimed at reversing a recent increase in smoking by minors.
LONDON - Amnesty International, the human rights charity, says it is launching its first billboard advertising campaign, aimed at raising awareness about the group among Britons under 30.

NEW DELHI - A leading Indian health organisation, the Voluntary Health Association of India, says it will step up a campaign this year against tobacco companies' sponsorship of sporting events. Tobacco advertising is banned on Indian television.
CHICAGO - Marks Bros. Jewelers Inc says it has retained Barkley & Evergreen, a full-service advertising and marketing firm.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - Just months after it won a legal battle to give it the right to broadcast up-to-the-second basketball scores over its pager network, Motorola Inc has stopped actively promoting the product, the New York Times says.
LONDON - EMAP Plc says it has received an approach from a potential buyer of a number of its business magazines including "UK Press Gazette" and "Media Week".

SYDNEY - The potential for pay television advertising in Australia is over-stated and it will be several years before it becomes a meaningful revenue stream, Australis Media Ltd chief executive Sean O'Halloran says.
LONDON - Shares in Grampian Television Plc leapt as the company confirms it is in talks with Scottish Media Group Plc which may lead to a merger of the two companies.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS, MARKETS & CONSUMER TRENDS:

NEW YORK - Coca-Cola Co's Powerade may soon be the sport drink of choice for the National Hockey League, the Wall Street Journal says. The company is expected to announce it has cut a $30 million deal to have Powerade named the official sports drink of the league, replacing Quaker Oats Co's Gatorade.
MUNICH - Computer Chip maker Intel Corp says it does not know why demand in Europe has unexpectedly softened and that it sees no signs competitors are gaining market share in the region.

LONDON - The collapse of communism in Central and Eastern Europe sent Western-based multinationals stampeding into the region, but experts say many have been burned by Europe's emerging consumer markets.
JOHANNESBURG - Daimler-Benz AG Chairman Juergen Schrempp says the company sees Africa as the market of the future.
TOKYO - Toyota Motor Corp declines to comment on an Indian media report that the company will invest $240 million in a joint venture with India's Kirloskar group.

TEGUCIGALPA, Honduras - The Association of Coffee Producing Countries plans to start coffee drinking promotions in countries such as Russia and China to boost consumption. A spokesman says "Massive campaigns are under consideration for countries such as Russia and China, among others, with the objective of promoting coffee".
